E — ComputeDriven Event / Analytics Plane

Opus Review + Implementation Brief — Workers + Queues + ClickHouse Cloud

Canonical public product/domain: e.computedriven.com Initial analytical freshness target: 2 hours Primary data plane: Cloudflare Workers + Cloudflare Queues + ClickHouse Cloud Future live plane: Durable Objects + WebSockets + Super Date: 2026-08-23 Status: architecture/review brief; Opus must inspect the current codebase before implementing

0. Product surface and domain

The public product surface is:

`e.computedriven.com`

It should contain:

e.computedriven.com
  ├── marketing
  ├── docs
  ├── app/dashboard
  ├── public API
  ├── SDK documentation
  └── canonical fallback ingest endpoint

For ComputeDriven-owned sites, prefer a first-party browser ingestion route on each site:

https://computedriven.com/_e/v1/events
https://opensentience.org/_e/v1/events
https://ampersandboxdesign.com/_e/v1/events
...

Those routes should terminate in Cloudflare and forward through a Worker/service binding to the same central E ingest logic.

External or non-Cloudflare integrations can later use:

https://e.computedriven.com/v1/events

or configure their own first-party proxy.

E is one coherent product surface. The ingest endpoint, developer documentation, dashboard, and eventual live-context experience should all be designed as parts of that product rather than as separate products.

1. Product thesis

E is not “our own Google Analytics.”

It is the event, journey, and live-context plane for ComputeDriven.

The long-term idea is:

Behavior should not end in a dashboard. It should become governed context that humans and agents can understand and act on while the user is still present.

The short-term system is deliberately simpler:

browser / server events
        |
        v
Cloudflare Workers
        |
        v
Cloudflare Queue
        |
        | buffered
        | every 2 hours
        v
ClickHouse Cloud
        |
        +----> E dashboard
        +----> PostHog
        +----> Amplitude
        +----> cached summaries
        |
        `----> later Super projections

The critical decisions are:

  • E owns the canonical semantic event contract.

  • E owns stable event IDs.

  • ClickHouse is an isolated analytics database from day one.

  • Existing ComputeDriven product databases are not part of this scaling/failure domain.

  • PostHog and Amplitude are downstream analytical lenses, not sources of truth.

  • Live session state will later live outside ClickHouse.

  • Historical analytical freshness starts at two hours, not seconds.

  • We deliberately learn Workers + Queues + ClickHouse now while mistakes are cheap.

2. Hard boundaries

2.1 Separate analytics data plane

Do not put E event tables in the existing ComputeDriven Pigsty deployment.

Do not use the Keycloak/PlanetScale database.

Do not create hidden cross-database coupling.

Conceptually:

COMPUTEDRIVEN PRODUCT PLANE
---------------------------
identity
accounts
organizations
worlds
runs
nodes
billing
product state
existing Pigsty / product stores

             |
             | emits approved semantic events
             v

E ANALYTICS PLANE
-----------------
Cloudflare Workers
Cloudflare Queues
ClickHouse Cloud
later Durable Objects
later R2 archive

The product plane may publish events such as:

signup_completed
workspace_created
world_created
build_completed
subscription_started
subscription_cancelled

but E must not require direct table reads from the product database to function.

2.2 ClickHouse is analytical truth, not transactional product truth

ClickHouse should hold:

  • accepted semantic events;

  • analytical session/journey facts;

  • attribution facts;

  • bot-intervention analytical events;

  • derived/materialized analytical views.

It must not become authoritative for:

  • auth;

  • organizations;

  • billing entitlement;

  • World authority;

  • secrets;

  • production mutations.

2.3 Live state is not ClickHouse state

Do not keep ClickHouse awake merely to answer:

who is on this page now?
what did this visitor click 3 seconds ago?
is chat open?
which component is visible?

Those are later Worker/Durable Object concerns.

ClickHouse initially answers:

what happened in the last 2h/day/week/month?
which journeys convert?
where do funnels fail?
which sources lead to signup?
which events predict activation?

5. Why a pull Queue + 2-hour Cron matters

Do not attach the canonical event queue to a normal push consumer if the objective is to let ClickHouse sleep.

A push consumer automatically consumes continuously. Delaying each message by two hours only creates a two-hour-offset continuous stream; after the initial delay it can still keep ClickHouse awake around the clock.

The intended V1 behavior is:

00:00 - 01:59   Queue accumulates
02:00           flush wakes ClickHouse
02:00-02:0x     drain queue + insert
02:0x           snapshot/materialized work complete
02:0x+idle      ClickHouse scales down

02:00 - 03:59   Queue accumulates
04:00           next flush
...

Use:

  • Cloudflare Queue configured with HTTP pull consumer;

  • Cloudflare Cron Trigger on a dedicated flush Worker;

  • cron expression conceptually every two hours;

  • scheduled Worker repeatedly pulls batches until:

  • queue is drained;

  • execution time budget is nearly exhausted;

  • ClickHouse failure occurs;

  • a safety/backpressure threshold is reached.

Cloudflare documents pull consumers specifically for cases where upstream consumption needs to be rate/availability controlled. Pull batch size currently supports up to 100 messages. Queue retention on Paid can be configured up to 14 days, giving ample recovery room for a 2-hour cadence.

Cron time

Cloudflare Cron Triggers run in UTC.

Do not encode business meaning into the exact UTC boundary. “Every two hours” is an operational flush interval, not a reporting-day definition.

6. Initial freshness SLO

V1 historical analytical SLO:

normal freshness target: <= 2h 15m

Reason:

  • up to ~2h wait before scheduled drain;

  • ClickHouse cold start;

  • drain/insert/materialization time;

  • cached dashboard snapshot publication.

Track:

oldest_unflushed_event_age_seconds
queue_depth
last_successful_flush_at
last_successful_event_occurred_at
clickhouse_flush_duration_ms
events_flushed
batches_flushed

Alert thresholds:

WARN     oldest event > 2h 30m
ERROR    oldest event > 4h
CRITICAL oldest event > 8h

The queue retention must be much longer than the critical threshold.

7. Browser batching

Do not equate CDN HTTP requests with analytics events.

Do not send one Worker request for every semantic event unless a specific event requires immediate delivery.

Preferred SDK behavior:

browser session
    |
    +-- event
    +-- event
    +-- event
    +-- event
    |
    v
microbatch
    |
    +-- timer
    +-- pagehide
    +-- size threshold
    v
/_e/v1/events

Initial targets:

max events per browser batch:       25
target payload:                      < 64 KB
hard payload cap:                    significantly below Worker/Queue limits
flush timer:                         15-30 seconds
flush on pagehide:                   yes
sendBeacon/keepalive fallback:       where appropriate

Why target under 64 KB:

Cloudflare Queue operations are metered in 64 KB chunks. Keeping a logical browser batch below that boundary makes cost and behavior simpler.

Do not obsess over exactly 25. Measure actual encoded event sizes and tune.

8. Canonical semantic event envelope

E owns the schema.

Suggested v1:

{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "event_id": "01J...",
  "event_name": "pricing_viewed",
  "occurred_at": "2026-08-23T16:30:00.000Z",

  "site_id": "computedriven",
  "domain": "computedriven.com",
  "path": "/pricing",

  "anonymous_id": "anon_...",
  "user_id": null,
  "account_id": null,
  "session_id": "ses_...",
  "journey_id": null,

  "source": {
    "referrer": "https://opensentience.org/...",
    "source_domain": "opensentience.org",
    "utm_source": null,
    "utm_medium": null,
    "utm_campaign": null
  },

  "context": {
    "locale": "en-US",
    "viewport_class": "desktop",
    "release": "git-sha"
  },

  "consent": {
    "analytics": true,
    "replay": false,
    "personalization": false
  },

  "properties": {
    "placement": "hero"
  }
}

Rules:

  • event_id is immutable.

  • Event names are stable snake_case.

  • Reject unsupported schema versions.

  • Never use email as the canonical user key.

  • user_id/account_id are opaque internal IDs.

  • Keep top-level fields tightly controlled.

  • Free-form properties have max nesting/bytes.

  • URLs/query strings are redacted/allowlisted.

  • Server strips known sensitive keys even if client validation fails.

  • Historical event semantics are never silently redefined.

10. ClickHouse Cloud V1

Use ClickHouse Cloud Basic initially unless repo/security requirements force Scale.

Current public AWS us-east-1 list pricing checked 2026-08-23:

Basic compute:  $0.2181 / compute unit-hour
Basic storage:  $25.30 / TB-month
Basic storage:  up to 1 TB
Basic memory:   8-12 GiB total
Basic AZs:      1

ClickHouse states that unused resources can scale down to zero.

This is intentionally a learning/starter deployment. Cloudflare Queues isolates event acceptance from ClickHouse availability.

Upgrade triggers to Scale should be measurement-driven:

need >1 TB
need stronger production availability
need 2+ AZ
need configurable memory / compute separation
need private networking
need workload isolation

Do not self-host ClickHouse yet merely to save tens of dollars.

The point of V1 is to learn:

  • schema design;

  • sort keys;

  • partitions;

  • inserts;

  • async inserts;

  • idempotency;

  • materialized views;

  • query behavior;

  • compression;

  • cost per million events;

  • cold starts;

  • scale-to-zero behavior;

  • operational failure modes.

11. ClickHouse client

For Worker access, use the official web/fetch client unless repo testing shows a reason not to:

@clickhouse/client-web

The official ClickHouse JavaScript client documents Cloudflare Workers compatibility.

Keep all ClickHouse access server-side.

Never ship ClickHouse credentials to browser code.

Create distinct ClickHouse users/roles:

e_ingest
  INSERT approved raw tables
  minimal SELECT if required for health
  no broad ALTER

e_query
  SELECT approved tables/views
  no INSERT
  no ALTER

e_admin
  migrations/schema
  tightly held

e_super            later
  SELECT only explicitly approved views

Do not give Super raw arbitrary SQL authority.

12. Initial raw table design

Opus should benchmark actual query patterns before freezing ORDER BY.

A candidate—not a final ruling:

CREATE TABLE events_v1
(
    event_id UUID,
    batch_id UUID,
    schema_version UInt16,

    event_name LowCardinality(String),

    occurred_at DateTime64(3, 'UTC'),
    received_at DateTime64(3, 'UTC'),

    site_id LowCardinality(String),
    domain LowCardinality(String),
    path String,

    anonymous_id String,
    user_id Nullable(String),
    account_id Nullable(String),
    session_id String,
    journey_id Nullable(String),

    source_domain LowCardinality(String),
    referrer String,

    context JSON,
    consent JSON,
    properties JSON
)
ENGINE = MergeTree
PARTITION BY toYYYYMM(occurred_at)
ORDER BY
(
    site_id,
    toDate(occurred_at),
    event_name,
    occurred_at,
    session_id,
    event_id
);

Benchmark alternatives based on real intended queries, especially:

events for one session
events for one user
events by site and time
events by event type and time
funnel sequences
source -> conversion
journey traversal
bot-assisted conversion

Write a short benchmark note before finalizing the key.

13. Queue message format

The Queue should carry microbatches, not single events.

Example:

{
  "batch_version": 1,
  "batch_id": "01J...",
  "site_id": "computedriven",
  "accepted_at": "2026-08-23T16:30:02.000Z",
  "events": [
    { "...": "..." },
    { "...": "..." }
  ]
}

Requirements:

  • one batch_id per accepted Worker microbatch;

  • every event also has its own event_id;

  • target message size <64 KB;

  • hard max event count;

  • hard max bytes;

  • invalid event handling is explicit;

  • never queue unchecked arbitrary payloads.

14. Two-hour flush algorithm

Pseudo-flow:

scheduled() every 2h
    |
    v
acquire flush lease / avoid overlapping drain
    |
    v
wake/query ClickHouse
    |
    v
repeat:
    pull <=100 queue messages
    if empty -> stop

    flatten validated event batches
    bound aggregate insert bytes/rows
    INSERT into ClickHouse

    if INSERT confirmed:
        ack pulled queue messages
    else:
        do not ack
        exit / allow visibility timeout
until time budget reached
    |
    v
refresh materialized/snapshot outputs if needed
    |
    v
write cheap dashboard freshness snapshot
    |
    v
end; ClickHouse becomes idle

Do not acknowledge first

Correct:

pull -> insert -> confirmed -> ack

Wrong:

pull -> ack -> insert

The wrong order can lose analytics on a failed insert.

Retry semantics

Assume at-least-once delivery.

Design ClickHouse insert/idempotency handling so a Worker crash after database success but before queue ACK does not silently duplicate analytical meaning.

Test this explicitly.

Do not claim “exactly once” unless the entire path actually proves it.

15. ClickHouse sleeping strategy

The database only stays cheap if E does not constantly wake it.

Therefore:

WRITE PATH
queue -> ClickHouse every ~2h

NORMAL PUBLIC READ PATH
cached snapshots / cheap edge state

DEEP ANALYTICS READ PATH
explicit ClickHouse query

At the end of a successful flush, publish summary data required for the ordinary dashboard to a cheap always-available layer.

Possible v1 choices after repo inspection:

Cloudflare KV
D1
Cache API
static JSON snapshot in R2 later

Do not build a second analytical database there.

Store only dashboard-serving summaries such as:

last_flush_at
events_last_24h
pageviews_today
signups_today
top_sites
top_pages
conversion snapshot
vendor delivery health

Opening the public E homepage should not wake ClickHouse.

16. Approximate early cost envelope

Do not promise these numbers. Measure them.

At the current portfolio traffic level, CDN requests are not equal to analytics events.

If semantic browser/server events are batched before entering Workers, Cloudflare should remain inexpensive.

Cloudflare Workers Paid currently lists:

$5/month base
10M Worker requests/month included
$0.30 per additional million requests
30M CPU-ms/month included

Cloudflare Queues Paid currently lists:

1M operations/month included
$0.40 per additional million operations
typical successful message ~= write + read + delete

ClickHouse Cloud Basic currently lists:

$0.2181 / compute unit-hour in AWS us-east-1
$25.30 / TB-month storage

The exact cost of a two-hour wake pattern depends on:

  • service size;

  • resume latency;

  • insert duration;

  • merge/background activity;

  • idle timeout;

  • dashboard queries;

  • batch size;

  • actual analytics event volume.

Initial engineering target:

keep the core E data plane in roughly the $10-$30/month range if real measurements support it, without sacrificing correctness merely to hit that number.

The software must expose actual:

ClickHouse active minutes/day
events per flush
bytes per flush
compressed bytes/event
Worker requests/month
Queue operations/month
cost per 1M accepted events

so future cost decisions are empirical.

17. PostHog and Amplitude fanout

The canonical chain should be:

browser
  |
  v
E ingress
  |
  v
Queue
  |
  v
ClickHouse accepted event
  |
  +---> PostHog
  `---> Amplitude

E is the semantic source of truth.

PostHog receives:

  • canonical semantic events;

  • plus its own high-resolution browser behavior/replay path where configured.

Amplitude receives:

  • curated canonical semantic events;

  • not raw behavioral exhaust.

Use stable E event_id downstream for dedup/reference.

Do not scatter direct semantic posthog.capture() and Amplitude calls throughout site code if they bypass E’s event contract.

Vendor-specific behavioral features may remain vendor-specific.

18. Identity model

Both PostHog and Amplitude must be able to see anonymous -> authenticated journeys.

Do not split:

guests -> PostHog
members -> Amplitude

Use:

before login:
anonymous_id = anon_x
user_id = null

after login:
anonymous_id = anon_x
user_id = usr_y

Record an identity link according to privacy policy.

On logout:

  • reset vendor identity state;

  • prevent a later browser user from inheriting the prior authenticated identity.

Never use email address as the analytics primary key.

19. Cross-domain portfolio journeys

Cookies do not become first-party across unrelated registrable domains.

Do not use fingerprinting or hidden third-party-cookie hacks.

For known portfolio links:

source domain
     |
signed short-lived journey token
     |
     v
destination domain
     |
local anonymous session linked to journey_id

The token:

  • contains no secrets;

  • contains no email;

  • expires quickly;

  • is signed;

  • is removed from the visible URL after exchange where practical;

  • cannot magically deanonymize unrelated traffic.

Example conceptual payload:

{
  "v": 1,
  "journey_id": "jny_...",
  "source_site": "opensentience",
  "source_session": "ses_...",
  "iat": 1787500000,
  "exp": 1787500600
}

20. First-party /_e routing

For ComputeDriven-owned Cloudflare zones, investigate a reusable deployment pattern:

domain.com/_e/*
        |
        v
zone Worker route
        |
        v
service binding to cd-e-ingest

Benefits:

  • first-party browser endpoint;

  • no cross-origin ceremony for our own sites;

  • less obvious third-party tracking hostname;

  • one central validation implementation;

  • site identity can be bound by route/config instead of trusting arbitrary browser input.

Security rule:

The ingest Worker should derive/verify site_id from trusted route/config where possible, not blindly trust client-supplied site_id.

Fallback:

e.computedriven.com/v1/events

for integrations where first-party routing is unavailable.

25. Privacy / consent

Define explicit categories:

analytics
replay
personalization
support_chat

Do not hardcode legal conclusions.

Engineering requirements:

  • browser consent API;

  • vendor initialization gated by policy;

  • replay separately governed;

  • server-side redaction even if client is buggy;

  • query-string allowlist/redaction;

  • deletion path by opaque identity;

  • retention policy configuration;

  • internal/bot traffic filtering;

  • privacy documentation based on implementation.

26. Security

Minimum requirements:

  • restrictive allowed origins for fallback cross-origin ingest;

  • first-party Worker routes where possible;

  • request body limits;

  • event count limits;

  • property nesting/size limits;

  • schema validation;

  • sensitive-key redaction;

  • rate limits;

  • bot/abuse handling;

  • Worker secrets for ClickHouse credentials;

  • separate ClickHouse users/roles;

  • TLS only;

  • no browser DB credentials;

  • no public admin SQL endpoint;

  • CSP on E website;

  • authenticated protected /app;

  • CSRF where browser state changes exist;

  • no sensitive event payloads in ordinary logs;

  • environment separation:

  • dev;

  • staging;

  • prod;

  • separate queues and ClickHouse DB/table prefixes per environment.

28. Tests / falsifiers

Do not ship the happy path only.

Ingest

  1. Invalid schema never reaches Queue.

  2. Unsupported schema version is rejected.

  3. Oversized batch is rejected.

  4. Oversized property object is rejected.

  5. Sensitive configured keys are stripped server-side.

  6. site_id cannot be spoofed on first-party routes.

  7. Duplicate event_id retry does not create double analytical meaning.

  8. Page navigation does not block waiting on analytics.

Queue / two-hour buffer

  1. Queue can accumulate for >2h without loss.

  2. Flush Worker does not run continuously.

  3. No push consumer exists on canonical buffered queue.

  4. Cron overlapping with previous drain is safely serialized or made harmless.

  5. Empty queue does not keep ClickHouse awake with useless work.

  6. Backlog survives a ClickHouse outage longer than one interval.

  7. Messages are not ACKed before successful DB insert.

  8. Worker crash after DB insert but before ACK is safe/idempotent.

  9. Visibility timeout causes safe redelivery.

  10. Backlog age alarms fire.

ClickHouse

  1. Candidate sort keys are benchmarked against representative queries.

  2. Materialized view failure behavior is understood/tested.

  3. Cold-start duration is measured.

  4. Idle scale-down is observed rather than assumed.

  5. Insert batch size is measured for throughput/cost.

  6. Raw event query remains correct across month partitions.

  7. Query user cannot INSERT.

  8. Ingest user cannot perform broad admin operations.

Identity

  1. Anonymous -> authenticated link works.

  2. Logout prevents identity bleed to the next user.

  3. Two users on one browser do not collapse.

  4. Cross-domain journey token expires.

  5. Tampered journey token fails.

  6. Unrelated anonymous visits are not automatically linked.

Vendor fanout

  1. ClickHouse succeeds while PostHog fails: canonical event remains valid.

  2. ClickHouse succeeds while Amplitude fails: canonical event remains valid.

  3. Vendor retry reuses E event ID.

  4. One vendor outage does not block the other.

Website

  1. E homepage does not wake ClickHouse under normal cached rendering.

  2. Dashboard indicates freshness timestamp.

  3. “live” UI never presents a two-hour snapshot as live.

  4. Synthetic demo data is visibly labeled.

  5. Privacy page corresponds to actual code.

Future Super seam

  1. Session projection excludes passwords/secrets.

  2. Unknown UI capability is rejected.

  3. Bot cannot execute arbitrary JS through capability API.

  4. Historical ClickHouse read permission does not imply product mutation authority.

31. Initial 2-hour cost hypothesis

Treat this as a hypothesis to falsify.

At current traffic:

  • Cloudflare CDN HTTP requests may be <700k/day.

  • This does not imply 700k analytics events/day.

  • Browser microbatching should keep Worker requests far below raw event count.

  • Queue microbatches should keep Queue operation volume modest.

  • ClickHouse two-hour flushes should create about 12 scheduled wake opportunities/day rather than continuous ingestion.

Potential early target:

Cloudflare Workers/Queues     low single digits to low tens/month
ClickHouse Basic              single digits to low tens/month if sleep behavior is favorable
Total core E plane            target roughly $10-$30/month

Again: measure real active minutes before claiming this publicly.

If ClickHouse is repeatedly kept awake by:

  • background work;

  • dashboard reads;

  • vendor fanout queries;

  • badly structured jobs;

fix the architecture before accepting a permanent 24/7 compute bill.

Do not create dozens of speculative views.

For normal E web rendering, write compact summary snapshots after each 2-hour flush.

The homepage/app should display:

Last analytics refresh: 10:02 UTC

or equivalent.

Freshness is a product property and should be visible.

34. Implementation sequence

Phase 0 — review only

  • inspect current codebase;

  • inspect DNS/Cloudflare;

  • inventory analytics;

  • produce conflicts/findings;

  • confirm domain routing.

Phase 1 — E shell

  • e.computedriven.com marketing shell;

  • docs/architecture/privacy placeholders;

  • CI/deploy;

  • no fake live data.

Phase 2 — schema + SDK

  • e-schema;

  • browser SDK;

  • first-party route proof on one ComputeDriven site;

  • validation/redaction tests.

Phase 3 — Queue

  • canonical e-events Queue;

  • producer;

  • microbatching;

  • paid retention configured;

  • no continuous push consumer.

Phase 4 — ClickHouse

  • Basic service;

  • roles/users;

  • candidate schemas;

  • benchmark;

  • final v1 schema/migrations.

Phase 5 — 2-hour scheduled drain

  • HTTP pull consumer;

  • Cron flush Worker;

  • idempotency;

  • backlog/failure tests;

  • measure scale-to-zero behavior.

Phase 6 — cached dashboard

  • post-flush summaries;

  • freshness timestamp;

  • public E dashboard does not wake ClickHouse.

Phase 7 — vendor adapters

  • PostHog;

  • Amplitude;

  • retries/delivery status;

  • canonical event ID mapping.

Phase 8 — portfolio rollout

  • add first-party /_e route to sites incrementally;

  • compare Cloudflare traffic to human pageviews;

  • build cost-learning dashboard.

Phase 9 — live/Super

Only after event system is stable:

  • Durable Objects;

  • WebSockets;

  • chat;

  • SessionProjection;

  • typed UI capability protocol;

  • Super bridge.

35. Do not build yet

Do not add:

  • Kafka;

  • self-hosted ClickHouse cluster;

  • R2 as a required hot-path dependency;

  • custom replay engine;

  • arbitrary browser-control agent;

  • full BI builder;

  • fingerprinting;

  • third-party-cookie hacks;

  • ClickHouse as product transaction DB;

  • second analytics Postgres;

  • a Phoenix backend unless the current codebase demonstrates a concrete need that Workers/Durable Objects do not satisfy;

  • 24/7 ClickHouse queries merely to make a dashboard look “real-time.”

R2 can be added later for:

cold archive
Parquet exports
reprocessing
training/research corpora
long retention

when those jobs are real.

ClickHouse:

  • Cloud pricing

https://clickhouse.com/pricing

https://clickhouse.com/cloud

  • Official JS client

https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js

Important currently verified facts:

  • Workers Paid includes 10M requests/month and then charges per additional million.

  • A Worker Cron Trigger can run scheduled jobs; triggers execute in UTC.

  • Queue pull consumers are intended for controlled consumption from upstream infrastructure.

  • Paid Queue retention can be configured up to 14 days.

  • Pull batch size currently supports up to 100 messages.

  • ClickHouse Cloud Basic is explicitly positioned for starter/testing projects.

  • ClickHouse Cloud advertises scaling unused compute down to zero.

  • The official @clickhouse/client-web client is compatible with Cloudflare Workers.

Do not freeze provider prices into product behavior. Prices are planning inputs only.

Unless codebase review produces a material contradiction, implement toward:

        E views  PostHog  Amplitude


                    LATER LIVE PLANE
                         |
                         v
                  Durable Objects
                         |
                    WebSockets
                         |
                  SessionProjection
                         |
                         v
                       Super

This deliberately gives E its own scaling and failure domain from the first real event.

The initial goal is not maximum scale.

The initial goal is to learn the correct scale architecture early:

edge acceptance -> durable buffering -> analytical batch ingest -> cheap historical queries -> live state somewhere else.

Break it while it is small. Measure everything. Preserve event identity. Fail without losing evidence.
